S1Result: A coding agent wrote a module and its own tests. Line coverage was one hundred percent.
Then a tool made seventy five small changes to the code. The tests caught sixty eight. Seven slipped through.
That is a mutation score of ninety point six seven percent.
One feedback round caught six more. Ninety eight point six seven percent. Here is how.
S2Setup: The task was a voucher engine. It applies discount codes to a shopping basket.
The spec is full of edges. Minimum spend. Expiry dates. Rounding. Caps. And stacking.
The agent was asked for the code and the tests it would ship. It got no hint of what came next.
In under three minutes it wrote ninety two lines and thirty one passing tests.
S3Mutants: Line coverage counts the lines a test runs. It never asks what the test checks.
Mutation testing changes one small thing in the code. Each changed copy is a mutant.
Here less than becomes less than or equal. Then the suite runs again.
A test fails. So the mutant is killed. If every test passes the mutant survived.
Stryker made seventy five mutants. Sixty eight were killed. Seven survived.
S4Survivors: Four survivors sit at a boundary or a tie or in the stacking rule. Two only blank an error message. The last one comes later.
Here less than zero became less than or equal to zero. Free items now throw an error. No test used a zero price.
Here greater than became greater than or equal. A tie now goes to the later voucher. No test had a tie.
Every one of these lines still ran. So line coverage stayed at one hundred percent.
S5Feedback: The seven survivors went back to the agent. It could change the tests only. The code was locked.
In about three minutes it wrote six new tests. Each one is named for the bug it prevents.
Thirty seven tests. Seventy four of seventy five mutants killed. Ninety eight point six seven percent.
S6Equivalent: The last mutant survived both rounds. The agent showed that no test could ever kill it.
This mutant swaps the first check for true.
With a minimum spend the first check is already true. Without one the second check compares a number with undefined. That is always false. Same result either way.
This is an equivalent mutant. The agent confirmed it by running the code. It suggested a skip comment instead of a junk test.
S7Takeaway: Coverage measured what the tests ran. Mutation testing measured what they checked.
So do not accept AI written tests on coverage alone. Feed the survivors back. Keep a person on the verdicts.
One caveat. One small module with a spec full of edges. One agent. One run. Try it on your own code before you trust the numbers.
S8EndCard: Every number and every test is in the public repo. The links are in the description.
